traceability.notes:
The story 006.0-DEV-FILE-VALIDATION is fully implemented and verified.
All acceptance criteria are met: - Core Functionality: The `valid-story-reference` ESLint rule inspects `@story` annotations, resolves candidate paths relative to `context.cwd`/project root and configured `storyDirectories`, enforces `.story.md` extension by default, and checks filesystem existence with caching. Tests assert valid references and report `fileMissing` when files are absent. - Quality Standards: Implementation follows ESLint rule patterns (sync FS operations wrapped in helpers, context-based cwd, schema-defined options) and never throws on FS operations, instead returning status objects and diagnostics. Error-handling behavior is exhaustively unit-tested with mocked FS failures. - Integration: The rule operates on `@story` comment lines whose format is validated by the separate annotation-format story (005.0). It uses consistent `@story` parsing (`handleComment` + `validateStoryPath`) and integrates into the plugin as a standard rule, so it can be combined with other traceability rules without conflict. - User Experience: Error messages `fileMissing`, `invalidExtension`, `invalidPath`, and `fileAccessError` are specific, include the offending path (and error text for FS issues), and are covered by tests that assert both messageId and contextual data. - Error Handling: Filesystem permission and I/O errors are handled via try/catch in `checkSingleCandidate` and surfaced as `fs-error`/`fileAccessError` diagnostics, not uncaught exceptions. Dedicated tests verify behavior for EACCES and EIO errors both at the utility and rule levels. - Documentation: docs/rules/valid-story-reference.md provides a full specification of behavior, path resolution rules, project boundary semantics, configuration options, and examples that align with the story’s requirements and examples.
All listed technical requirements (REQ-FILE-EXISTENCE, REQ-ERROR-HANDLING, REQ-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION, REQ-PATH-RESOLUTION, REQ-SECURITY-VALIDATION, REQ-PERFORMANCE-OPTIMIZATION, REQ-PROJECT-BOUNDARY, REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATHS) have concrete implementations with corresponding passing tests. Therefore, this story is assessed as PASSED.
